Grade 4 · Unit 4.2

Circuits and Energy Conversion

How can we make a safe circuit that changes electrical energy into useful light?

Concept 1

A circuit is a complete loop

Electric current flows only in a closed path.

Analogy

Train track

a looped track with a small train.

“If the track is broken, the train stops. If the wire path breaks, the current stops.”

Try it

Light the LED

coin cell, LED, tape, and foil strips.

“Connect the battery to the LED in a loop. The LED lights. If it stays dark, flip the LED. It works one way.”

Diagram

Open vs closed

one circuit with a gap and one circuit without a gap.

“Open path: no light. Closed path: light.”

Data

LED direction log

a table with LED direction, Lights? yes/no.

“Try both ways. Record which way lights.”

Concept 2

Conductors and insulators

Some materials let current flow easily; others do not.

Try it

Material tester

paper clip, foil, string, plastic, wood placed in the circuit gap.

“Put each material in the circuit. Does the LED light?”

Data

Conductor table

table with Material and Lights? columns, plus real observation log.

“Metals conduct. Plastic does not. Real log: test each material. Provided dataset: paper clip yes, foil yes, string no, plastic no, wood no.”

Real world

Safe wiring

metal wire inside plastic coating.

“Metal carries current. Plastic coating keeps it safe.”

Concept 3

Switches open and close circuits

A switch controls whether the circuit is complete.

Try it

Paper clip switch

two brass fasteners and a paper clip.

“Move the clip to touch both fasteners. The light turns on.”

Diagram

Switch open and closed

switch touching one fastener, then both.

“Open switch: path broken. Closed switch: path complete.”

Real world

Flashlight

flashlight switch.

“A flashlight has a switch inside.”

Concept 4

Circuits convert energy

Electrical energy can change into light, sound, motion, or heat.

Diagram

Energy conversion

battery to LED with arrows: electrical → light + a little heat.

“The battery gives electrical energy. The LED makes light.”

Try it

Light-up card

paper card with foil path and LED.

“Close the switch. The card lights up. Electrical energy became light energy.”

Real world

Doorbell

button and bell.

“Electric energy becomes sound.”

Hands-on · Design or investigate

Try it at home or in class

Design a “light-up card” with a switch. Criteria: the light turns on when the switch is closed. Constraints: one coin cell, one LED, foil or copper tape, paper. Students test, find why it fails if it is dark, and refine the circuit.

Try it

What you need

coin cells, small LEDs, copper tape or aluminum foil, binder clips, paper clips, brass fasteners, index cards, tape, paper, pencil.

Safety: coin cells only; never wall current. Tape over coin cells when stored. Check LED orientation; the LED lights only one way. A small LED can run straight from one coin cell because the cell limits the current; never use a bigger battery or wall power. If foil or a coin cell feels warm, unhook it right away: a wire joining both ends of the cell is a short circuit and gets hot. An adult hands out and collects every coin cell; a swallowed coin cell is a medical emergency. Check battery freshness. If magnets are used for extensions, keep magnets away from Chromebooks.

Try it

What you do

Build a simple circuit. Test conductors and insulators. Make a paper-clip switch. Design and refine a light-up card.

Words to know

circuit
a complete path for electric current.
current
moving electric charge.
battery
device that provides electrical energy.
conductor
material that lets current flow easily.
insulator
material that blocks current.
switch
device that opens or closes a circuit.
open circuit
broken path; no current.
closed circuit
complete path; current flows.
energy conversion
energy changing form.
LED
a small light that uses electric current and works one way.
Tutor notes: misconceptions, standards, pacing

Pacing: five 30-minute sessions.

Common misconceptions to listen for:

  • “Electricity is used up in the bulb.” Correct: energy transfers; current flows in a loop.
  • “One wire is enough.” Correct: a complete path is needed.
  • “The battery stores current like water.” Correct: batteries store chemical energy; current is moving charge.
  • “All circuits are dangerous.” Correct: small battery circuits are safe, but wall electricity is dangerous.
  • “LEDs work either direction.” Correct: LED lights only one way; flip it if it is dark.
  • “Plastic and wood conduct electricity like metal.” Correct: metals conduct; plastic and wood are insulators.
  • “An open switch still lets current flow.” Correct: an open switch breaks the path.

Limits and cautions:

  • 4-PS3-2 is partly earned here; sound, light, and heat transfer belong in 4.1.
  • Coin cells are safe for this grade, but they are a swallowing hazard for younger siblings; tape them when stored.
  • LEDs can stay dark if reversed or if the battery is weak; check orientation and battery freshness.
  • The unit does not teach voltage, series/parallel circuits, or current measurement.

Michigan Science Standards this unit earns:

  • 4-PS3-2: Observe that energy can be transferred by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
  • 4-PS3-4: Apply scientific ideas to design, test, and refine a device that converts energy from one form to another.

Connections: Builds on: Unit 0: How Science Works; 2-A Materials and Their Uses; 4.1 Energy, Speed, and Collisions. Builds toward: Unit 8.3 Forces at a Distance; Unit 8.2 Energy Transformation & Conservation; Unit 13 Energy Resources & Human Impact.
